papers.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
papers.summary: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. The specific contact resistance for base is estimated 1.32 x 10^{-2} Ohm.cm^2. The open-base breakdown voltage is characterized ~63 V for a 300 nm collector without dielectric passivation. This work lays the foundation for future development of N-polar III-Nitride HBTs for next-generation RF applications.

papers.title: 8-in. wafer-scale uniform growth of GaN-on-silicon epilayers for near-eye micro-displays
papers.summary: Heteroepitaxial growth of high-quality gallium nitride (GaN) films and their uniform light-emitting diode (LED) structures on 8-in.-wafer-scale silicon (Si) substrates remains a significant challenge due to large lattice and thermal mismatches for the critical control of threading dislocations (TDs) and wafer bowing. Here, we proposed a novel variable growth rate strategy to grow a 6.7-μm-thick, crack-free GaN layer on an 8-in. Si(111) substrate. By carefully managing the thermal stress and the interactions between TDs during epitaxial growth, we could reduce the TD density to approximately 8.0 × 107 cm−2, thereby implying very high-quality GaN epi-layers on Si substrates compared to previous reports. Moreover, blue LED structures were grown on this GaN template, exhibiting a standard deviation of 1.1 nm in peak wavelength and a wafer bowing of 16 μm over the entire 8-in. wafer. This epi-wafer was finally used to fabricate micro-LED arrays via direct 8-in. wafer bonding, revealing the great potential of GaN-on-Si techniques for near-eye micro-displays.

papers.title: Deep-level defect in GaN diodes observed with electrically detected magnetic resonance
papers.summary: Point defects continue to limit the performance of GaN and other III–V semiconductor devices. The dominant electrically active defects in GaN are predicted to be vacancies such as VGa and VN and their complexes with common impurities such as O and H. Electrically detected magnetic resonance (EDMR) is a powerful technique for detecting the physical and chemical nature of electrically active point defects which affect the performance of semiconductor devices. We show, to our knowledge, the first room temperature EDMR on GaN displaying hyperfine structure. The EDMR spectrum has a g⊥c=2.005±0.001, g∥c=2.006±0.001, |ΔI/I0|=8×10−6, and a 10-line hyperfine structure. We identify the observed defect, with reasonable certainty, as the VGa−VN divacancy.

papers.title: High-quality GaN epilayer grown on Si substrates enabled by a SiO2-frustum-patterned template
papers.summary: GaN-on-Si technologies have attracted considerable attention for next-generation electronic applications, yet high threading dislocation density (TDD) remains a major challenge. Here, we develop a SiO2-frustum-patterned template for effective filtering of threading dislocations (TDs) in wafer-scale GaN-on-Si heteroepitaxy. The SiO2 array blocks the directly upward propagation of TDs through the masked zones, while the window zones promote lateral overgrowth and facilitate rapid TD bending and termination. To further suppress coalescence-related TDs, facet-evolution regulation is introduced to promote highly ordered domain coalescence, with a misorientation angle of only 0.088°. Consequently, a TDD of 5.4 × 107 cm−2 is achieved in a 4.2-μm-thick GaN epilayer grown on a 4-in. Si substrate, substantially lower than that of conventional GaN-on-Si heteroepitaxy. This work demonstrates a low-cost solution for high-quality GaN-on-Si heteroepitaxy, providing a promising material platform for high-performance GaN-based power electronics.

papers.title: Polarity-driven divergence in thermal decomposition of GaN: Kinetics, morphology, and surface damage recovery
papers.summary: Although the polarity-dependent thermal decomposition of gallium nitride (GaN) has been studied, the fundamental mechanisms that govern decomposition morphology and kinetics remain unclear. In this work, the distinct thermal decomposition behavior of gallium (Ga)-polar and nitrogen (N)-polar GaN was systematically investigated. Notably, thermal etching produces grooved hexagonal inverted pyramids on N-polar GaN but hexagonal pyramids protrusions on Ga-polar GaN, a difference that is clearly elucidated by a facet-dependent etching rate model. By employing a growth–etching–regrowth approach, the activation energies under H2/NH3 ambient are measured as 2.88 ± 0.25 eV for Ga-polar GaN and 2.50 ± 0.15 eV for N-polar GaN. Despite its lower activation energy, N-polar GaN etches more slowly than Ga-polar GaN due to a much smaller pre-exponential factor that imposes significant kinetic constraints. In comparison, under N2/NH3 ambient, Ga-polar GaN exhibits an activation energy of 3.40 ± 0.065 eV, while N-polar GaN behaves highly resistant to thermal etching with an etching rate below 5 nm/h even at 1050 °C. Beyond kinetics, thermal treatment effectively removes the dry-etch-induced surface damage, with N2 ambient providing superior recovery for both polarities. These findings not only clarify polarity-dependent decomposition pathways but also provide practical guidelines for interface engineering in high-performance GaN devices.

papers.title: Gate-length dependence of trap passivation via rapid deuterium annealing in scaled MOSFETs
papers.summary: As the semiconductor industry pursues higher integration density and faster operating speeds, the physical gate length (LG) of metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) continues to scale down. This aggressive scaling exacerbates short-channel effects, which require proportionally thinner gate dielectrics to improve gate controllability. However, gate dielectrics are highly susceptible to electrical stress, making gate oxide reliability a critical concern. While conventional forming gas annealing is widely employed to improve dielectric quality, its high thermal budget can induce thermal damage in advanced scaled devices. Rapid deuterium annealing (RDA) has emerged as a promising alternative to minimize this thermal budget and mitigate thermal degradation. Nevertheless, the efficacy of the RDA process across different LG values remains unexplored. To address this, we investigate the gate-length dependence of RDA on device performance. Planar Si nMOSFETs were fabricated on bulk substrates, and key device parameters were systematically extracted and analyzed using I–V and C–V measurements.

papers.title: Quantum-dot-assisted AlGaN wide-bandgap tunnel junction enabling high-reflectivity electrodes for deep-ultraviolet LEDs
papers.summary: AlGaN deep-ultraviolet (DUV) light-emitting diodes (LEDs) suffer from limited light extraction efficiency due to high absorption losses in the p-GaN contact layer and annealed metal layers for p-type Ohmic contact. Here, we boosted the DUV reflectivity by incorporating a p-GaN quantum-dot-assisted AlGaN tunnel junction on top of the AlGaN LED epitaxial structure. Precisely controlled thermal decomposition of the top p-GaN layer is realized in a high-vacuum chamber, which transforms the conformal p-GaN layer into nanopyramid-shaped quantum dots by eliminating over 95% of the p-GaN. Subsequent in situ molecular beam epitaxy regrowth of a smooth wide-bandgap n-AlGaN contact layer enables tunneling injection of holes and lateral current spreading. The resulting device exhibits a low specific contact resistivity of 2.5 × 10−5 Ω cm2 and a tunnel-junction voltage drop of 1.09 V. Moreover, the n-AlGaN top contact allows the use of a low-coverage Ti/Al/Ni/Au grid electrode combined with an Al reflector, increasing the effective reflectance at 265 nm to 77.16%. These results demonstrate that the p-GaN quantum-dot-assisted AlGaN tunnel junction improves electrical injection characteristics and enables a high-reflectivity electrode architecture, which promises improved light extraction in AlGaN DUV LEDs.
